source_review.notes: Checked all ten final NASA and NIST references on 2026-08-31; every URL returned HTTP 200. Reviewed NASA Configuration Management and CM Plan guidance, SWE-081 configuration-item identification, NIST SP 800-128, Technical Data/Requirements/Interface Management, Product Verification, Phase E configuration practices, and NPR 7123.1B. NIST security-focused scope and NASA-specific governance are kept explicit.

evidence: Reviewed configuration graph C_t=(N,L,B,E,P) and each component definition.
Reviewed authorized transition C_t to C_(t+1) under change, authority, impact, and verified implementation.
Reviewed CI tuple, change-request tuple, observed state C-hat by time/site, and drift set difference.
Confirmed identity, revision, variant, instance, lot/serial, build, release, deployment, and state are not overloaded.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation consistently represents configuration as typed items and relationships with baseline, effectivity, provenance, and actual state.

evidence: Executed configuration-identity-fixture under python3 with exact output in artifacts/snippets/SYSENG-083/report.json.
Confirmed eight declared and observed dimensions, seven initial exact matches, and data_schema mismatch.
Confirmed mismatch forces reject_configuration_mismatch under the declared toy gate.
Confirmed correction yields eight exact matches and only eligibility for the metadata gate.
Recomputed Exercise 2 naive coverage 10/12=83.333...%.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Exact-string counts do not establish artifact content, provenance, semantics, runtime loading, security, behavior, or authorization.

evidence: Confirmed declared version/release identity does not entail complete system configuration.
Confirmed approval does not entail implementation, rollout, verification, closure, or universal effectivity.
Confirmed source/declarative configuration does not entail observed physical/runtime state.
Confirmed a digest identifies bytes under an algorithm but does not entail provenance, loading, semantic compatibility, correctness, or suitability.
Confirmed emergency speed changes workflow latency but does not eliminate identity, authority, evidence, reconciliation, or retirement duties.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The chapter uses implication limits and counterexamples rather than claiming metadata equality proves configuration integrity.

evidence: Challenged CI granularity, identifier collisions/overloading, renames, variants, serials/lots, environments, mutable tags, stale links, and hidden/generated items.

Challenged hardware materials/process/supplier/firmware/calibration, software toolchains/dependencies/images, data/schema/models/reference tables, infrastructure/policy/secrets/flags, and human/procedure/facility configurations.
Challenged interfaces/shared ownership, supplier/platform change, emergency work, partial/offline fleets, spares, field repairs, mixed versions, compatibility, rollback, and old-version retirement.
Challenged manifest-generator/control-system compromise, weak provenance, declared/observed drift, automatic remediation evidence loss, retention/privacy/security, and archival tool obsolescence.
Reviewed all ten examples and five complete answers for assumptions, intermediate reasoning, evidence limitations, and bounded conclusions.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Real configuration assurance requires applicable design, software/data/infrastructure, manufacturing/supplier, interface, operations/maintenance, safety/security, records, CM, verification, and technical-authority expertise.

evidence: Confirmed every CI/control record has identity, ownership, lifecycle state, provenance, authoritative source, relationships, effectivity, and retention.
Confirmed configuration scope includes end and enabling products across physical, digital, data, human, facility, supplier, evidence, and retirement surfaces.
Confirmed proposal, assessment, approval, implementation, verification, rollout, closure, and retirement remain distinct states.
Confirmed as-designed/built/tested/delivered/deployed/maintained states are captured and reconciled.
Confirmed status accounting answers intended/actual/change/authority/effectivity/evidence/open-work questions.
Confirmed drift, unauthorized/incomplete change, control-system integrity, recovery, and archival are monitored/audited.
invariant_checking.notes: No version label, Git repository, digest, manifest, part number, board approval, deployment dashboard, or deletion event is treated as sufficient alone.

proof_review.notes: No formal proof or theorem requires proof review; the module presents configuration relations and bounded metadata checks.

proof_sketch_labeling.notes: No passage is labeled or presented as a proof sketch.

evidence: Executable output is labeled synthetic_exact_string_comparison_only.
Fixture limitations disclaim contents, signatures, provenance, semantics, runtime state, hidden configuration, authority, security, and behavior.
Examples and exercises are teaching cases, not actual CM audits, supply equivalence approvals, deployments, or security authorizations.
Official sources are attributed without claiming NASA/NIST review or endorsement.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Synthetic comparison, source-backed guidance, internal review, configuration audit, technical authority, and operational authorization remain distinct.

conceptual_review.notes: Internal conceptual review checked configuration/CI/baseline/effectivity distinctions, identification, item granularity, identifiers, relationships, authoritative baselines, actual-state views, change proposal/impact/authority/transition, status accounting, verification, drift, recovery, and retirement.

practitioner_review.notes: Internal practitioner-oriented review checked physical/software/data/infrastructure configurations, multi-party ownership, normal/preapproved/emergency controls, provenance, builds/supply, rollout cohorts, field/spare effectivity, observation/discovery, health metrics, control-system protection, audits, archives, and incident use.

pedagogical_review.notes: Internal pedagogical review confirmed progression from item selection and identity through control, realization, observed state, audit and retirement. Ten examples and five complete solutions cover parts, releases, interfaces, field repair, infrastructure, ML/data, evidence transfer, hotfixes, fleets, and retirement.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external NASA/NIST expert, configuration manager, design authority, supplier, manufacturer, software/data/platform owner, operator/maintainer, safety/security authority, records/privacy authority, auditor, or other external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
